source.title: On the generalization of learning algorithms that do not converge
source.authors: N. Chandramoorthy; Andreas Loukas; Khashayar Gatmiry; S. Jegelka

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and references.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training and test errors and examines how loss dynamics and statistical stability relate to their gap under label corruption. It does not test the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, or model-size comparisons.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own CIFAR-10 label-corruption experiments on VGG16 and ResNet18: estimated statistical stability, test loss autocorrelation, and training–test error gap. The VGG16 autocorrelation/gap comparison is reported in Figure 3 as described in text; the ResNet18 stability results and gap context appear in Appendix D. Other claim versions are not directly evaluated.
record.test_reason: The study tests statistical algorithmic stability and loss autocorrelation as predictors of generalization, which are different constructs from V1–V8. Partial label corruption up to p=0.5 does not establish V1's coexistence of nearly perfect random-label fitting and natural-label generalization. No listed architecture, width, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal comparison is performed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors extend algorithmic stability to time-averaged loss statistics, prove generalization bounds under their assumptions, and report empirical associations between statistical stability, loss dynamics, and generalization. Autocorrelation is explicitly a heuristic proxy, not a definitive predictor.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies time-averaged loss statistics and statistical algorithmic stability, not the interventions or measurements in the listed claim versions. Experiments use SGD with momentum 0.9, fixed learning rate 0.01, batch size 128, and CIFAR-10 label corruption.
record.method_sensitivity: Label-corruption probability changes estimated stability and generalization error; the generalization gap is larger at intermediate corruption and decreases at p=0.5 when training error also rises.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated lower bounds on the statistical stability coefficient increase with label corruption for VGG16 and ResNet18, accompanying worse held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested fixed-recipe CIFAR-10 training conditions, sensitivity of time-averaged test loss to training-data perturbations tracks held-out performance across corruption levels.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet18 test-loss autocorrelation magnitudes preserve the ordering of the generalization-gap estimates across corruption levels. The gap decreases at p=0.5 because training error is also large; its ratio to test error falls from approximately 80% at p=0 to 20% at p=0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-loss autocorrelation can serve as a heuristic indicator of time-averaged generalization gaps in these non-convergent SGD runs.

record.problems: The experiments use only VGG16 and ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with fixed optimizer settings. The autocorrelation is explicitly described as a heuristic proxy, and several numerical comparisons are shown only in figures. The high-corruption case cannot fit training data well, complicating the generalization-gap pattern.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The exact plotted values for stability, test error, and autocorrelation are not stated in the text and are therefore recorded as figure only.

untested.parts: No comparison demonstrating nearly perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error; the NTK discussion does not establish the claimed test-error trend.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison or tuning comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout intervention, training-set-size comparison, or joint dropout and weight-decay removal.

No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measurements or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The toy example's curvature is not this measure and has no generalization-gap comparison.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows and not-tested version assessments. Its gate note also incorrectly attributes Figure 3's autocorrelation/gap comparison to VGG16; Figure 3 concerns ResNet18. No failure of V1 is inferred from incomplete fitting at 50% corruption under this different recipe.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization comparison.
No model-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison to norm- and margin-based measures.

relation.reason: The study discusses generalization, flat minima, and related training findings, while developing and evaluating a distinct stability framework.

tranche.reason: The study measures statistical algorithmic stability and loss dynamics, which do not test V1–V8. Partial label corruption does not establish V1; its toy curvature analysis does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization-gap relationship.

source_check.notes: Figure 3's caption and prose interchange the autocorrelation and gap panel references; exact figure values are unavailable in the supplied text. Appendix D defines the gap estimator as the time average of absolute test–training error differences and specifies a 200-epoch run-up before Figure 5's 1200-epoch averaging window.
